publishedWalks.title: Highgate Walk in London — A Lady in London
stops: Swain’s Lane and Highgate Cemetery, with optional entry
themes: Residential architecture, green spaces, independent shops and pubs
Advertised as a two-to-three-hour linear walk, not a one-hour Highgate station loop
stories: Primarily a place-discovery itinerary rather than a historical narrative; advertises cemetery notables including Karl Marx and views from Parliament Hill. Locator: route and details, lines 26–95. Publisher-owned travel blog; URL indicates September 2022, but revision date is unverified. ([aladyinlondon.com](https://www.aladyinlondon.com/2022/09/highgate-walk.html))

publishedWalks.title: The Highgate Village Self-Guided Walk — Richard Jones
stops: South Grove and St Michael’s Church
stories: Advertises Dickens family lodgings in 1832, the inn custom of swearing on horns, Coleridge’s residence and treatment, and Dickens connections at Ivy House and the Whittington Stone. These remain the guide’s claims, not independently verified narration evidence. Locator: lines 51–200; publication date not established. ([london-walking-tours.co.uk](https://www.london-walking-tours.co.uk/free-tours/highgate-village-walk.htm))

publishedWalks.title: Highgate Village and Cemetery London Walk — Joolz Guides
stories: The accompanying webpage advertises the Highgate vampire, Pond Square’s ghost chicken, Flask ghost and highwayman tales, swearing on horns, and Highpoint’s television associations. Catalogue only: supernatural and celebrity claims are not accepted as historical fact. Locator: lines 37–59; publication date unknown. Video not played. ([joolzguides.com](https://joolzguides.com/videos/highgate-village-cemetery-walk/))

publishedWalks.title: Waterlow Park — sylviaszekely, Go Jauntly
stops: Advertised farmers’ market at St Joseph’s Catholic Primary School
themes: Sunday leisure, food and park exploration
stories: Advertises market shopping, a park stroll and a roast rather than historical stories. Only six preview steps are public on the opened page; the complete route requires the app. Current market operation and the final meal location were not verified. Locator: lines 15–49; publication date unknown. ([walks.gojauntly.com](https://walks.gojauntly.com/walks/waterlow-park-14806895149008687591?cId=172))

publishedWalks.title: North Hill, Highgate — architectural walk
themes: Housing design, light, materials and charitable provision
North Hill corridor rather than a station loop
stories: Highlights Highpoint’s modernism, Segal’s deliberately understated house, and separate household entrances at Veranda Cottages. Selected advertised stops, not the complete inventory. Locator: PDF page 1, numbered building entries; filename carries 20 May 2020, not a verified publication date. Council-hosted interpretive leaflet. ([haringey.gov.uk](https://www.haringey.gov.uk/sites/haringeygovuk/files/attachment_north_hill_architectural_walk_20_may_2020.pdf))

candidates.name: Highgate Underground station — public exterior bookend
candidates.why: Required start and finish. Proposed discovery: the everyday station as wartime refuge. Lauderdale House’s institutional history reports local people sleeping in Highgate tube during the Blitz; use as an attributed research proposition, not proof of which platforms or entrance were involved. Locator: The Blitz, lines 36–39. Present anchor: a station exterior, exact exit and safe standing position unresolved. No underground view promised. ([lauderdalehouse.org.uk](https://www.lauderdalehouse.org.uk/about-us/our-history/blitz))

candidates.name: Highpoint — North Hill frontage
candidates.why: Proposed contrast to picturesque village imagery: explain modern apartment design through an exterior view. The architectural leaflet identifies Lubetkin and Tecton and International Modernism, PDF page 1, Highpoint entry. Proposed standing point is the public pavement, not gardens, driveway or entrance canopy. Visibility and exact position require checking; do not repeat the leaflet’s factory-worker occupancy claim without corroboration. ([haringey.gov.uk](https://www.haringey.gov.uk/sites/haringeygovuk/files/attachment_north_hill_architectural_walk_20_may_2020.pdf))

candidates.name: 9 North Hill — Walter Segal’s house
candidates.why: An alternative architectural candidate about restrained design rather than grandeur. The leaflet identifies Segal’s own 1965 house and says it is concealed behind garages, PDF page 1, entry 7. Proposed anchor: whatever is genuinely visible from North Hill pavement. Reject if the view cannot support discovery; do not enter private access or imply this house demonstrates his later self-build system without further evidence. ([haringey.gov.uk](https://www.haringey.gov.uk/sites/haringeygovuk/files/attachment_north_hill_architectural_walk_20_may_2020.pdf))

candidates.name: Veranda Cottages — 61–83 North Hill
candidates.why: A housing-history alternative to famous residents. The leaflet describes charitable flats with individual external entrances, PDF page 1, entry 20. Proposed discovery: how access arrangements reveal separate households. Anchor: frontage seen from public pavement, never residents’ stairs. Its speculative explanation invoking later bye-laws needs resolution; the additional northward distance may exclude this candidate from the hour. ([haringey.gov.uk](https://www.haringey.gov.uk/sites/haringeygovuk/files/attachment_north_hill_architectural_walk_20_may_2020.pdf))

candidates.name: The Gatehouse — village junction
candidates.why: Proposed discovery: the relationship between a village name, land ownership and movement through a toll gateway. Both Jones and Joolz advertise that association; this is a corroboration lead, not established medieval-site evidence. Locators: Jones lines 74–77; Joolz lines 52–53. Anchor: exterior and junction from a safe public pavement position, not a pub interior or carriageway. Distinguish the present building from the earlier gateway. ([london-walking-tours.co.uk](https://www.london-walking-tours.co.uk/free-tours/highgate-village-walk.htm))

candidates.name: Pond Square — vanished water and remembered place
candidates.why: A legible public-space candidate requiring little prior knowledge: investigate why a square retains the name of missing water. Jones states that the water source was filled in in 1864, line 84; that date remains uncorroborated. Anchor: a public standing point within the square, to be specified. Prefer landscape change over repeating the ghost-chicken story as fact. ([london-walking-tours.co.uk](https://www.london-walking-tours.co.uk/free-tours/highgate-village-walk.htm))

candidates.name: The Wrestlers — inn customs from outside
candidates.why: Proposed discovery: how a drinking ritual bestowed a playful local identity. Joolz advertises swearing on horns at this inn, lines 54–58. Investigate historical documentation and distinguish past practice from present operation; no performance, interior artefact or purchase is promised. Anchor: pub frontage from public pavement, exact stopping space unresolved. ([joolzguides.com](https://joolzguides.com/videos/highgate-village-cemetery-walk/))

candidates.name: Lauderdale House — reuse, fire and community recovery
candidates.why: A supported alternative to royal gossip: the house’s institutional history describes hospital use, park staff accommodation, the 1963 fire and reopening as an arts centre in 1978. Locator: Our History, lines 115–118. Proposed discovery: how a grand house acquired public uses. Anchor: exterior from a public park path, with a visible architectural detail selected later; no interior admission required. ([lauderdalehouse.org.uk](https://www.lauderdalehouse.org.uk/about-us/our-history))

candidates.name: Upper Waterlow Park — Joy Hunt’s remembered view
candidates.why: An unusually specific local account: Lauderdale House’s webpage recounts Joy Hunt looking over burning London with her father during the Blitz, lines 45–49. Proposed discovery connects an ordinary park view with a named resident’s recollection. Present-day viewpoint must be independently selected; the webpage does not locate her exact position or date. Attribute the memory and do not invent sensory detail. May merge with the house stop. ([lauderdalehouse.org.uk](https://www.lauderdalehouse.org.uk/about-us/our-history/blitz))

candidates.name: Highgate Cemetery — Swain’s Lane exterior
candidates.why: A familiar landmark considered as an exterior-only reserve, not a compulsory attraction. Published walks advertise cemetery history and famous burials, but neither graves nor interior monuments should be promised from the street. Proposed discovery would concern the cemetery’s relationship to the hillside and neighbourhood after fresh institutional verification. Anchor: a safe public pavement position outside the gates. The downhill diversion and return climb require measurement before inclusion. ([aladyinlondon.com](https://www.aladyinlondon.com/2022/09/highgate-walk.html))
